gaps.explanation: Re-read pp6-7 (Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Fund Balances, modified accrual, 7 fund columns + Total) and pp11-17 (one 'Budget and Actual (Budget Basis)' schedule per fund). Every statement fund column has its own schedule in detail (no missing column, no missing schedule page, no fund recorded twice; the Sewer Fund lines are business-type). JSON statement total 36,014,357 = printed Total revenues p7 (no statement issue). Total revenues per fund, statement vs schedule Actual: General 26,620,390 (p6) vs 23,757,807 (p11) = 2,862,583 (taxes: statement Property 10,434,311 + Sales and use 6,280,036 + Occupation 2,862,255 + Motor vehicle 510,937 + In lieu 200,977 = 20,288,516 vs schedule 'Taxes' 19,044,812; Grant income 1,759,638 on the schedule vs Intergovernmental 5,286,640 on the statement); Debt Service 4,663,794 vs 4,035,939 (p14) = 627,855 (Sales taxes 3,140,021 vs 2,514,631); Keno 1,293,761 vs 1,250,728 (p12) = 43,033; Capital Improvements 11,780 vs 11,780 (p15) = 0; Economic Development 28,758 (p7) vs 13,916 (p16) = 14,842; 84th Street 3,166,745 (p7) vs 2,702,970 (p17) = 463,775 (Sales taxes 3,140,020 vs 2,676,259); Police Academy 229,129 vs 229,128 (p13) = 1. Sum 4,012,089 = gap. Each schedule states 'Basic differences (accruals) occur because the cash basis of accounting used for budgeting differs from the modified accrual basis' and reconciles to the statement's Net Change on a GAAP Basis. Nothing printed is missing and nothing is counted twice; the difference is the report's own budget-basis vs GAAP figures. No fix.
